title: Micro-agenda: evals lint & triage
content:
Objective: quick, repeatable triage for the current quality regression affecting the Optimize eval runs. This note is the 1:1 / micro-sync prep I will use with Aisha/Priya before the broader sync. Keep it short: questions, hypothesis checklist, and immediate action items.

Context summary (TL;DR):
- During nightly evals (2026-08-02 02:00 UTC) the baseline redwood-7b-q4 quantized variant showed a ~12% drop in the 'factuality' metric on the financial prompt-set (finance-qs-v2). Embeddings similarity and toxicity signals unchanged. A/B cohort: redwood-7b-q4 (canary) vs redwood-7b-q4-quant (control).
- Suspected surface area: prompt preprocessing changes (recent prompt-normalizer update), or quantization kernel selection fallback.
- Impact: 1 customer sandbox reported noisy outputs in a billing-expense categorization test; overall downstream user impact currently low but risk of regression if rollout continues.

Quick diagnostic checklist (run in this order):
1) Re-run failing eval subset locally with --seed=42 and --no-batching to isolate nondeterminism. Command: "rdw-eval run --suite finance-qs-v2 --model redwood-7b-q4 --subset failing_cases.json --no-batch --seed 42 --out debug-run.json"
2) Compare token-level logprobs vs control for a small sample (first 20 failing cases). Use script: tools/compare-token-probs.py debug-run.json control-run.json
3) Recompute prompt-normalizer diff: git diff upstream/main -- src/prompt_normalizer.py; run normalized prompts through staging normalizer to check tokenization shifts.
4) Run inference with older kernel-binding (force-legacy-kernel flag) to test kernel selection hypothesis.
5) Check KV-cache warmup statistics in night-run logs (path: s3://redwood-evals/nightly/2026-08-02/). Look for increased cache misses.

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1 (most likely): prompt normalization edge-case changed for currency abbreviations (e.g., 'USD$' -> 'USD $') causing subtle token boundary shifts and changed logits.
- H2: quantization kernel fallback caused lower-precision matmul on specific layer shapes, affecting factual completions in finance domain.
- H3: batching behavior change (new global batcher tweak) caused input ordering or padding differences for short prompt sequences.

Data to collect before broader sync (quick wins):
- 10-case diff table: case_id, prompt_before, prompt_after, top3 tokens changed, token_prob_delta, output_diff (1-line). (owner: Quentin, due: EOD 2026-08-03)
- Kernel binding trace for night run and one manual run (owner: Isaac, due: 2026-08-03 11:00 PDT)
- Normalizer unit test coverage for currency/amount tokens and tokenizer snapshot (owner: Priya, due: 2026-08-03)

Proposed micro-actions for the 1:1 with Aisha (what I want from manager):
- Quick sign-off to pause the canary rollout if we confirm >10% degradation across the finance prompt family.
- Approval to spin a targeted A/B with forced-legacy-kernel for just the failing cohort (48h) and promoted traffic fallback.
- Request SRE to increase log retention for the failing night-run to 14 days (so we can correlate infra events).

Meeting agenda (10–15 min micro-sync):
- 0:00–02:00: 1-sentence recap + severity (Quentin)
- 02:00–06:00: show 3 representative failure cases and immediate diffs (screenshare)
- 06:00–10:00: choose action path (pause canary vs run quick A/B) + assign owners
- 10:00–15:00: blockers, infra asks, and communication (customer note draft)

Communication notes (if we need to inform customer sandbox):
- Keep it factual, no technical blame; acknowledge regression in 'test environment', note we are rolling a targeted canary pause and will follow up with results within 48 hours. Draft line: "We're seeing a mismatch in generated category labels for a subset of finance prompts in our sandbox. We're pausing the canary and running a short A/B test with a kernel rollback to identify root cause; will update within 48 hours."

Follow-up action items (flattened, for quick paste into task tracker):
- QH: assemble 10-case diff table + upload debug-run.json to S3 (s3://redwood-evals/debugs/quentin/2026-08-03) (due 2026-08-03 EOD)
- PD: add unit tests for currency tokenization, push tokenizer snapshot to artifacts (due 2026-08-03 noon)
- IR: produce kernel-binding trace + run forced-legacy-kernel test (due 2026-08-03 11:00 PDT)
- AK: approve pause plan if threshold met + coordinate customer comms (ASAP after diagnostic)
- SRE: extend log retention for night-run bucket to 14 days (ticket INF-3421) (owner: SRE oncall)

Notes-to-self for 1:1 delivery style:
- Be terse; show one failing case first then the metric table. Avoid jumping into deep kernel details unless asked. Have the technical artifacts linked in Slack ahead of the meeting.
- If manager asks for risk numbers, show projected rollback exposure delta (expected token-cost difference) and customer sandbox count (currently 2).

Open questions (to resolve in triage):
- Can we reproduce the exact token boundary shift outside of quantization paths? If yes, that points at prompt-normalizer and tokenizer behavior.
- Any infra deployments/driver rollouts overlapping 2026-08-01 -> 2026-08-02 window? (check release-engineering)

Backups / longer-term items (not urgent for micro-sync):
- Add an automated prompt-lint step in nightly eval pipeline that flags tokenization deltas > 0.05 KL divergence between normalizers.
- Expand eval harness to capture top-k token skyline snapshots for each case to make regressions easier to triage.

End of note. Will paste the important links to Slack thread before the 1:1.
